name: THOMPSON, Phillip Bruce, OAM

headline.note: Primary and contemporary sources establish Australian Army service from 2006, post-service veteran advocacy, a veteran peer-support management role by 2015 and selectability management by 2017. Published material does not establish Thompson's exact Defence separation, hours, leave or the complete boundaries and workload of his nonprofit roles. Elected office, nonprofit employment, governance and volunteer advocacy are excluded; no full-time public/private headline total is calculable.

career_spells.employer: Australian Army, 1st Battalion, Royal Australian Regiment
career_spells.evidence_note: The Australian of the Year profile says Thompson enlisted at 17 in 2006. His first speech says he was posted to 1 RAR at Townsville that year and deployed to East Timor in 2007 and Afghanistan in 2009. Official member biographies corroborate Army and 1 RAR service. A secondary biographical compilation gives 2006-2012 service, but an exact separation date and primary personnel record were not found.
career_spells.counting_note: Public service is established, but exact appointment and separation dates, hours, medical leave and the post-injury service interval are unresolved.

career_spells.employer: Veterans peer-support pilot program, employing entity not identified
career_spells.evidence_note: A contemporaneous Royal Australian Regiment Association director biography says Thompson became manager of a veterans peer-support pilot program in 2015. His official biography more generally says he worked for mental-wellbeing and suicide-prevention organisations after leaving Defence. The program and employing entity, exact start and end, hours and leave are not identified.
career_spells.counting_note: The role is treated as nonprofit employment pending employer-control evidence and is excluded from headline totals.

career_spells.role: Manager; exact program or title not fully identified
career_spells.evidence_note: The Royal Australian Regiment Association biography says Thompson became a manager of selectability, described as a North Queensland community mental-health organisation, in 2017. Federal Hansard in September 2017 independently identifies him as 'from selectability'. Official biographies say he worked in mental wellbeing and suicide prevention before Parliament. Exact dates, title, hours, leave and campaign arrangements are not published.
career_spells.counting_note: Nonprofit employment is excluded from public/private headline totals.

career_spells.role: Level 2 pensions and welfare advocate; mental-health and suicide-prevention advocate
career_spells.evidence_note: The Australian of the Year profile describes volunteer listening and veterans' employment, health and wellbeing advocacy. The RAR Association biography identifies Level 2 pensions and welfare advocacy. Sources do not separate paid work from volunteer advocacy across this interval.
career_spells.counting_note: Only explicitly unpaid or unresolved advocacy is represented here; it is excluded and must not be double-counted with nonprofit employment.

career_spells.evidence_note: The Association's August 2017 national-organisation page and Thompson's official biography identify him as a director. ACNC records confirm the Corporation is a registered charity. Exact appointment and cessation dates, remuneration and workload are not published.
career_spells.counting_note: Nonprofit governance is excluded and must not be double-counted as substantive employment.

career_spells.evidence_note: Thompson's official biography lists a directorship of Swiss 8, described as an online suicide-prevention application. Appointment dates, remuneration, workload and overlap with employment are not supplied.
career_spells.counting_note: Governance is excluded pending evidence that it was separate substantive paid employment.

career_spells.employer: Bravery Trust, Queensland Day and Australia Day programs
career_spells.evidence_note: The official biography lists the three ambassador roles but gives no dates, remuneration or workload. They are retained as unresolved community roles rather than assumed employment.
career_spells.counting_note: Ambassador roles without evidence of substantive paid employment are excluded.

career_spells.role: Member of the House of Representatives for Herbert
career_spells.evidence_note: Official parliamentary records show Thompson was elected to the House of Representatives at the 18 May 2019 federal election.

research_notes: Obtain a primary Defence personnel source for exact enlistment, medical leave and separation dates, hours and service status; 2012 is presently only a secondary-source endpoint.

Obtain selectability appointment, title, exact start and cessation, hours, leave and 2018-2019 candidate-period arrangements.
